439	        """Open and pin the leased object, asserting its identity matches."""
440	        fd = os.open(os.fspath(self.path), os.O_RDONLY)
441	        try:
442	            st = os.fstat(fd)
443	            if (st.st_dev, st.st_ino) != (self._leased_dev, self._leased_ino):
444	                raise OSError(
445	                    errno.ESTALE,
446	                    "wal object identity changed under the exclusive lease: %r"
447	                    % (str(self.path),),
448	                )

451	            raise

454	    def _acquire_lease(self):
455	        """Take the exclusive write lease for this store's real log object.
456	
457	        The lease has three cooperating flocks, all held per open file
458	        description so two exclusive instances conflict even within one
459	        process, and all released by the kernel when the holder dies:
460	
461	        * a legacy sibling lock derived from the normalized absolute path,
462	          preserving the original same-spelling mutual exclusion;
463	        * an identity lock named by the real object's (st_dev, st_ino), so
464	          symlink and hard-link aliases of one existing log compete for the
465	          very same lease instead of each getting its own path lock;
466	        * for a log that does not exist yet, a creation gate named by the
467	          canonical target path that serializes concurrent first opens
468	          across aliases. After acquiring it the path is re-resolved: the
469	          first opener creates the log and adopts its inode lock, while any
470	          alias opener that finds the object already there -- or created by
471	          the first opener -- takes (or loses on) the inode lock.
472	
473	        Nothing here reads, creates, truncates, or appends WAL bytes; only
474	        metadata and side-channel lock files in a shared lock directory are
475	        touched. A conflict raises WalBusyError; an unresolvable identity or
476	        failing file operation propagates the underlying OSError.
477	        """
478	        # 1. Legacy per-path sibling lock: unchanged path, message, and
479	        # mutual exclusion for identical normalized spellings.
480	        self._lock_fd = self._take_flock(
481	            os.path.abspath(os.fspath(self.path)) + ".lock"
482	        )
483	        try:
484	            identity = self._identity_stat()
485	            if identity is not None:

552	    def _adopt_created_identity(self, write_fd):
553	        """Adopt the inode lock for a log the gate winner just created.

556	        slipped past its own gate, so the fresh inode cannot already be

567	        self._pin_object()

569	        self._gate_fd = None

577	    def _verify_leased_object(self, f):
578	        """Guard every write-mode WAL open against an identity swap.
579	
580	        An exclusive store only ever mutates the exact (dev, ino) it leased;
581	        if the path was replaced (unlinked and re-created as another object
582	        through an alias) the write aborts with OSError rather than touching
583	        a log this instance never leased. Non-exclusive stores are unaffected.
584	        """

586	            return

588	        if (st.st_dev, st.st_ino) != (self._leased_dev, self._leased_ino):

590	                errno.ESTALE,
591	                "wal object identity changed under the exclusive lease: %r"
592	                % (str(self.path),),

635	    def _authorize_write_handle(self, f):
636	        """Pin every write-mode WAL handle to the leased real object.
637	
638	        If the creation gate is still held (the log did not exist when this
639	        exclusive store opened), opening for write is the first-create
640	        moment: adopt that object's inode lease then. Otherwise the handle
641	        must target the exact (dev, ino) the store leased; an identity swap
642	        aborts with OSError. Non-exclusive stores hold neither and are
643	        untouched.

650	    def _revalidate_for_append(self):
651	        """Validate the whole log by the exact recover rules before appending.
652	
653	        A store can stay open while its log is appended to or damaged out of
654	        band, so the boundaries cached when the store opened are never trusted
655	        for a write: the log is replayed from the head exactly as recover()
656	        does, re-determining valid_bytes, committed_bytes, and the last
657	        committed state. The replay builds only local objects, so a terminated
658	        invalid record, a blank/whitespace record, illegal UTF-8, duplicate or
659	        missing fields, an unknown op, a bad key/value, or a seq break raises
660	        WalCorruptionError without appending, truncating, or adopting anything
661	        -- state, commit_seq, and the byte boundary a later rollback observes
662	        are all left untouched.
663	
664	        The only bytes allowed beyond the replayed valid_bytes are the single
665	        trailing interrupted-write fragment the recovery rules recognise; that
666	        fragment is removed in place exactly as before, while every complete
667	        record before it -- legal uncommitted set/delete records included -- is
668	        preserved byte for byte. Returns the replayed committed view and the
669	        last committed seq in the file; the next record must use
670	        ``committed + 1`` rather than any seq cached at open time.
671	        """
672	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
673	        saved_boundary = self._valid_size
674	        saved_chain_head = self._chain_head
675	        try:
676	            (
677	                candidate,
678	                committed,
679	                _pending_count,
680	                valid_size,
681	                _committed_size,
682	            ) = self._replay()
683	            file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
684	            if file_size > valid_size:
685	                # The replay has already proved the bytes beyond valid_size
686	                # are exactly one unfinished tail fragment -- anything else
687	                # raised WalCorruptionError above -- so removing them can
688	                # never discard a complete, terminated record.
689	                with self.path.open("r+b") as f:
690	                    self._authorize_write_handle(f)
691	                    f.truncate(valid_size)
692	                    f.flush()
693	                    os.fsync(f.fileno())
694	        except BaseException:
695	            # Neither a failed validation nor a failed fragment removal
696	            # adopts a boundary: state, commit_seq, the cached
697	            # accepted-prefix edge, and the cached integrity chain head
698	            # stay exactly as on entry. Every later write revalidates from
699	            # the head in any case.
700	            self._valid_size = saved_boundary
701	            self._chain_head = saved_chain_head
702	            raise
703	        return candidate, committed

705	    def _append(self, row):
706	        """Durably append one log record after head-to-tail revalidation.
707	
708	        The whole log is validated under the exact recover rules first (see
709	        _revalidate_for_append); WalCorruptionError propagates with the file
710	        and in-memory state untouched. The record's seq is stamped from the
711	        seq replayed out of the file -- the file's last committed seq plus
712	        one -- never from a value cached when the store opened, so a batch
713	        committed out of band while the store was open extends the chain
714	        instead of being overwritten.
715	
716	        Raises OSError if the record cannot be written or synced; the
717	        un-durable tail is best-effort truncated back so a failed write can
718	        never masquerade as a committed record on reopen, and no new state is
719	        adopted before the record is durable.
720	        """
721	        candidate, committed = self._revalidate_for_append()
722	        record = dict(row)
723	        record["seq"] = committed + 1
724	        if self._protected:
725	            # Chain the record onto the integrity digest replayed out of
726	            # the accepted prefix (the seed for an empty log), exactly as
727	            # the replay recomputes it: the canonical core line is the
728	            # record without its integrity metadata, JSON-serialised with
729	            # sorted keys.
730	            core_line = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)
731	            record[_INTEGRITY_FIELD] = _chain_digest(self._chain_head, core_line)
732	        line = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
733	        created = not self.path.exists()
734	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
735	            self._authorize_write_handle(f)
736	            saved_size = f.tell()
737	            try:
738	                f.write(line)
739	                f.flush()
740	                os.fsync(f.fileno())
741	            except OSError:
742	                try:
743	                    f.truncate(saved_size)
744	                    f.flush()
745	                    os.fsync(f.fileno())
746	                except OSError:
747	                    pass
748	                raise
749	            new_size = f.tell()
750	        # Adopt only once the appended record is complete and durable.
751	        # candidate is the last *committed* view -- pending records never
752	        # join it -- so a set/delete append keeps the state deferred until
753	        # commit exactly as before, while a batch committed out of band
754	        # converges memory with what a reopen would recover.
755	        self._valid_size = new_size
756	        self.state = candidate
757	        self.commit_seq = committed
758	        if created:
759	            self._fsync_parent_dir()
760	
761	    def _fsync_parent_dir(self):
762	        """Best-effort persistence of a freshly created log file's directory entry."""
763	        try:
764	            fd = os.open(str(self.path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
765	        except OSError:
766	            return
767	        try:
768	            os.fsync(fd)
769	        except OSError:
770	            # Some filesystems do not support fsync on directories; the log
771	            # contents themselves have already been synced.
772	            pass
773	        finally:
774	            os.close(fd)

791	    def commit(self):
792	        # Re-validate the whole log and persist the commit boundary first; the
793	        # seq is stamped from the replayed last commit, and the new seq/state
794	        # are adopted only once the record is durable: a failed validation or
795	        # write must neither consume a seq nor present a committed state.

801	    def rollback(self):
802	        # Validate the log by the exact recovery rules before touching
803	        self._check_writable()
804	        # anything. The replay builds only local objects, so corruption raises
805	        # WalCorruptionError without partially replacing state or commit_seq.
806	        # committed_size is the byte offset just past the last commit record;
807	        # every complete set/delete beyond it is the uncommitted batch, and any
808	        # bytes beyond valid_size are the discardable interrupted-write tail.
809	        (
810	            _candidate,
811	            _committed,
812	            pending_count,
813	            _valid_size,
814	            committed_size,
815	        ) = self._replay()
816	        if not self.path.exists() or self.path.stat().st_size <= committed_size:
817	            # Nothing sits beyond the committed prefix (pending_count is then
818	            # necessarily 0); no truncation is needed.
819	            self._valid_size = committed_size
820	            return pending_count
821	        # Shrink the log in place: bytes of the committed prefix are never
822	        # rewritten or reordered, only the tail beyond the last commit is
823	        # removed. Persist before returning, and let an OSError from open,
824	        # truncate, flush, or fsync propagate -- a failed truncation must
825	        # never masquerade as a successful rollback. state and commit_seq are
826	        # not touched: they already equal the last committed view.
827	        with self.path.open("r+b") as f:
828	            self._authorize_write_handle(f)
829	            f.truncate(committed_size)
830	            f.flush()
831	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
832	        self._valid_size = committed_size
833	        return pending_count

835	    def restore(self, target_seq):
836	        """Commit the state of a past commit boundary as a fresh new state.
837	
838	        Read-only with respect to history: no earlier record is rewritten
839	        or reordered, and snapshot/history still serve every old commit.
840	        The target state is reached by one new set/delete batch sealed by
841	        one new commit, whose seq is latest commit_seq + 1 even when the
842	        target equals the current state (an empty batch then) or is 0
843	        (an empty state). Returns the new commit_seq.
844	
845	        target_seq must be a non-boolean non-negative integer no greater
846	        than the latest committed seq; type errors, negatives, and
847	        out-of-range values raise ValueError before the log is touched.
848	        The log is then validated under the exact recover/snapshot rules
849	        (corruption anywhere raises WalCorruptionError), and must be
850	        settled at the last commit: complete uncommitted set/delete
851	        records or a trailing unfinished fragment make it raise
852	        WalPendingError with the file, state, and commit_seq untouched.
853	        Every change record and the commit are appended and fsynced one
854	        at a time as in set/commit; an OSError propagates with the old
855	        committed state and seq in place, already-written records simply
856	        forming the batch's pending tail (rollback clears them).
857	        """
858	        self._check_writable()
859	        if (
860	            isinstance(target_seq, bool)
861	            or not isinstance(target_seq, int)
862	            or target_seq < 0
863	        ):
864	            raise ValueError(
865	                "target_seq must be a non-negative integer, got %r"
866	                % (target_seq,)
867	            )
868	        # Full recover/snapshot validation first, purely into local
869	        # objects: corruption raises before any truncation or append.
870	        history_views = []
871	        candidate, committed, pending_count, _valid_size, _committed_size = (
872	            self._replay(snapshots=history_views)
873	        )
874	        if target_seq > committed:
875	            raise ValueError(
876	                "target_seq %r exceeds latest committed seq %r"
877	                % (target_seq, committed)
878	            )
879	        # The log must be settled: neither a complete, terminated
880	        # uncommitted batch nor an unfinished tail fragment may be spliced
881	        # into. A tail fragment is recover/audit-recognised garbage the
882	        # next append would truncate away; refusing here keeps restore
883	        # from appending (or truncating) anything before validation has
884	        # fully passed, and forces the caller to commit, rollback, or
885	        # repair explicitly.
886	        file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
887	        if pending_count > 0 or file_size > self._valid_size:
888	            raise WalPendingError(
889	                "log is not settled at commit %r: %r pending record(s), "
890	                "an unfinished tail fragment is present"
891	                % (committed, pending_count)
892	            )
893	        current = candidate
894	        target = {} if target_seq == 0 else dict(history_views)[target_seq]
895	        # Merge the two key sets and write deterministically in Unicode
896	        # (code point) key order. A key only in the target, or present
897	        # with a different value under JSON-type-aware comparison, is a
898	        # set; a key present now but absent in the target is a delete.
899	        new_seq = committed + 1
900	        for key in sorted(set(current) | set(target)):
901	            if key not in target:
902	                self._append({"op": "delete", "key": key, "seq": new_seq})
903	            elif key not in current or not _json_equal(current[key], target[key]):
904	                # Deep copy: the adopted value must not share objects with
905	                # the replay's snapshot, which the caller could mutate.
906	                self._append(
907	                    {
908	                        "op": "set",
909	                        "key": key,
910	                        "value": copy.deepcopy(target[key]),
911	                        "seq": new_seq,
912	                    }
913	                )
914	        self._append({"op": "commit", "seq": new_seq})
915	        # Adopt the new committed view only once its commit boundary is
916	        # durable, exactly as commit() does.
917	        self.recover()
918	        return self.commit_seq

920	    def apply_batch(self, base_seq, changes):
921	        """Atomically commit an ordered batch of set/delete changes.
922	
923	        Every change is appended to the log first, in the caller's order,
924	        and the batch is sealed by one new commit record whose seq is the
925	        latest committed seq + 1 -- exactly as if the caller had issued the
926	        same set/delete records one at a time and then committed. Returns
927	        the new commit_seq. An empty changes collection is an empty commit:
928	        no change records, one commit record, seq advancing by one.
929	
930	        base_seq is the caller-declared compare-and-swap precondition: it
931	        must be a non-boolean non-negative integer and must equal the log's
932	        latest committed seq, otherwise the call raises ValueError or the
933	        unique WalConflictError respectively. Each change must be a dict
934	        carrying exactly the existing record semantics -- {"op": "set",
935	        "key", "value"} or {"op": "delete", "key"} -- with a string key and
936	        a value under the existing JSON-compatibility rules; any other
937	        shape raises ValueError. All argument validation completes before
938	        the log is touched.
939	
940	        The log is then validated under the exact recover rules (any
941	        corruption raises WalCorruptionError) and must be settled at the
942	        last commit: complete uncommitted set/delete records or a
943	        recover/audit-recognisable unfinished tail fragment raise
944	        WalPendingError. None of these rejections writes, truncates, or
945	        alters in-memory state. A read-only instance raises
946	        WalReadOnlyError and a closed one WalClosedError before any of the
947	        above, exactly as the other mutating entries do.
948	
949	        The write phase follows the same single-writer lease, per-record
950	        flush+fsync, and seq monotonicity rules as set/delete/commit: an
951	        OSError from any change record or the final commit propagates
952	        unchanged, the already-durable prefix stays observable through
953	        pending_changes and removable through rollback, and neither the
954	        in-memory state nor commit_seq advances. A process terminated at
955	        any write boundary recovers to the last complete commit on reopen;
956	        the unsealed part of the batch is never applied. Values are
957	        deep-copied into the written records, so neither the caller's
958	        changes collection nor the returned seq shares mutable nested
959	        objects with the store.
960	        """
961	        self._check_writable()
962	        if (
963	            isinstance(base_seq, bool)
964	            or not isinstance(base_seq, int)
965	            or base_seq < 0
966	        ):
967	            raise ValueError(
968	                "base_seq must be a non-negative integer, got %r" % (base_seq,)
969	            )
970	        if not isinstance(changes, (list, tuple)):
971	            raise ValueError(
972	                "changes must be a list of change records, got %r"
973	                % (type(changes).__name__,)
974	            )
975	        # Validate and normalize every change up front: a rejected call
976	        # must never create, truncate, or append to the log or alter
977	        # in-memory state. Values are deep-copied so the written records
978	        # can never share mutable nested objects with the caller's
979	        # collection.
980	        normalized = []
981	        for index, change in enumerate(changes):
982	            if not isinstance(change, dict):
983	                raise ValueError(
984	                    "change %r must be a dict, got %r"
985	                    % (index, type(change).__name__)
986	                )
987	            op = change.get("op")
988	            if op == "set":
989	                if set(change) != {"op", "key", "value"}:
990	                    raise ValueError(
991	                        "set change %r must carry exactly op, key and value, "
992	                        "got %r" % (index, sorted(change))
993	                    )
994	                _validate_key(change["key"])
995	                _validate_value(change["value"])
996	                normalized.append(
997	                    {
998	                        "op": "set",
999	                        "key": change["key"],
1000	                        "value": copy.deepcopy(change["value"]),
1001	                    }
1002	                )
1003	            elif op == "delete":
1004	                if set(change) != {"op", "key"}:
1005	                    raise ValueError(
1006	                        "delete change %r must carry exactly op and key, "
1007	                        "got %r" % (index, sorted(change))
1008	                    )
1009	                _validate_key(change["key"])
1010	                normalized.append({"op": "delete", "key": change["key"]})
1011	            else:
1012	                raise ValueError(
1013	                    "change %r has unknown op %r: only 'set' and 'delete' "
1014	                    "records may be batched" % (index, op)
1015	                )
1016	        # Full recover-rule validation of the log, purely into local
1017	        # objects: corruption raises WalCorruptionError before anything is
1018	        # written, truncated, or adopted.
1019	        (
1020	            _candidate,
1021	            committed,
1022	            pending_count,
1023	            _valid_size,
1024	            _committed_size,
1025	        ) = self._replay()
1026	        # The log must be settled at the last commit before a new batch is
1027	        # spliced on: neither complete uncommitted records nor a
1028	        # recognisable unfinished tail fragment may be present (same rule
1029	        # as restore).
1030	        file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
1031	        if pending_count > 0 or file_size > self._valid_size:
1032	            raise WalPendingError(
1033	                "log is not settled at commit %r: %r pending record(s), "
1034	                "an unfinished tail fragment is present"

1036	            )

1046	        new_seq = committed + 1
1047	        for change in normalized:
1048	            record = dict(change)
1049	            record["seq"] = new_seq

1053	        # durable, exactly as commit() does.
